questions.q: How is an invoice that is 'stuck on hold' different from one that fails to validate (Lesson 4)?
options: There is no difference; both are the same status
A held invoice has not yet been entered into the system
A held invoice has successfully validated but is blocked from payment by a specific named hold
A held invoice has already been paid
questions.explain: The invoice in this ticket validated successfully — it is not Incomplete — but carries a Price hold that blocks payment until released.

questions.q: What does a 'Price' hold on a PO-matched invoice indicate?
options: The supplier's bank account is invalid
The invoice has not been validated yet
The accounting period is closed
The invoiced price exceeds the purchase order price by more than the allowed tolerance
questions.explain: A Price hold is placed when the invoiced unit price exceeds the PO price beyond the configured tolerance percentage.

questions.q: In the Cascade Outdoor Supply ticket, why was updating the purchase order the correct fix rather than manually releasing the hold?
options: The price increase was legitimate, so fixing the PO resolves the cause for this and every future invoice from that supplier
Manual release is not technically possible in Oracle Fusion
The invoice price was actually wrong, not the PO
Updating the PO is always required before any hold can be viewed
questions.explain: Since the supplier's price increase was real, correcting the PO fixes the actual cause; manually releasing the hold would only clear this one invoice while leaving the PO wrong for future shipments.

questions.q: What happens to the cost difference if a Price hold is manually released instead of fixing the underlying variance?
options: It is automatically refunded to the supplier
It posts to a variance account instead of the expected charge account
It is deleted from the system with no accounting impact
It triggers an automatic PO price update
questions.explain: Manually releasing a matching hold does not resolve the variance — the price difference posts to a variance account rather than the intended charge account.

questions.q: Which hold would most likely be triggered if an invoice's tax amount does not match what Oracle calculates from the configured tax rate?
options: Qty Rec
Account hold
Tax Variance
Price
questions.explain: A Tax Variance hold is specifically for cases where the invoice's tax amount doesn't match the amount calculated from the configured tax rate.
